_comment: Competitive tiers, used as the primary input to Pokémon pricing.
FORMAT: DOUBLES (VGC). Champions is a doubles game — 4v4, bring six pick four — and the
doubles meta is very different from singles. Incineroar is S tier here on utility (Intimidate,
Fake Out, pivoting) while a singles list puts it mid-table; Hisuian Samurott is the reverse.
If your league plays singles instead, replace these lists with a singles tier list — nothing
Edit freely: this is the commissioner's balance lever, and house rules beat any public list.
Names are matched case-insensitively against each roster entry's species name, regional-form
label, Mega label and alternate-form label, so 'Wash Rotom', 'Alolan Ninetales' and
'Mega Charizard Y' all resolve. Anything that fails to match is reported by
`npm run roster:build` rather than ignored, so typos surface immediately.
`baseTiersIncludeMegas` says whether the tiers above already account for a species' Mega.
This doubles source does — Staraptor is S precisely because of Mega Staraptor — so Mega
tiers are shown for information but must NOT promote the species again, or Eelektross gets
counted as S twice over. If you swap in a tier list that ranks base forms only, set this to
false and each species will inherit the best tier its Megas reach.
Anything absent is `defaultTier` (UR), and is priced on base stats instead — see
source: Game8 Pokémon Champions doubles tier list, cross-checked against championscalc doubles usage rankings (Regulation M-B/M-C), captured 2026-09-11

megaTiers._comment: Megas ranked on their own merit. Only the S tier is published by the source; the rest inherit their base species' tier for display purposes.
